title: QBI Deduction with the Wage Limit, plus Net Investment Income Tax (2026 baseline)
scenario: Priya is single and materially participates in an S corporation that operates a NON-service (non-SSTB) manufacturing business. For 2026 the business allocates $400,000 of qualified business income to Priya, and the S corporation paid $120,000 of W-2 wages; there is no qualified property (UBIA = $0). Priya's taxable income before the QBI deduction is $500,000, which is above the 2026 threshold, so the full wage limitation applies. Separately, Priya has $50,000 of net investment income and modified AGI of $500,000. Apply the 2026 Public Law 119-21 baseline (QBI 20% deduction permanent; NIIT threshold $200,000 single) and round to the nearest dollar.

exhibits.label: Exhibit A — QBI and investment data

tasks.prompt: Requirement 1 — Compute the tentative QBI deduction (20% of qualified business income, before any limitation).
tasks.explanation: Tentative QBI deduction = 20% × $400,000 QBI = $80,000, before applying the wage/UBIA and taxable-income limits.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 2 — Compute the W-2 wage limitation (greater of 50% of W-2 wages, or 25% of W-2 wages plus 2.5% of UBIA).
tasks.explanation: Wage limit = greater of 50% × $120,000 = $60,000, or 25% × $120,000 + 2.5% × $0 = $30,000. The greater is $60,000. Because taxable income is above the threshold, this limitation applies in full.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 3 — Compute Priya's allowable QBI deduction.
tasks.explanation: Allowable QBI deduction = lesser of the tentative deduction ($80,000), the wage limit ($60,000), and 20% of taxable income ($100,000) = $60,000. The wage limitation is binding.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 4 — Compute Priya's net investment income tax.
tasks.explanation: NIIT = 3.8% × the lesser of net investment income ($50,000) or the MAGI excess over the $200,000 single threshold ($500,000 − $200,000 = $300,000). The lesser is $50,000, so NIIT = 3.8% × $50,000 = $1,900.
